body_ar:
هل القدس ستحرر ومن سيحررها وفي أي زمن؟

نعم سيفتح بيت المقدس، وقد بين النبي (ص) أن فتح بيت المقدس يحصل عند خراب المدينة، وأن ذلك يحصل بعده فتح رومية ويخرج الدجال في الثامنة، أي في السنة الثامنة بعد ذلك،

فيفتح بيت المقدس في الحرب الأولى مع اليهود، واليهود بقي معهم حربان الحرب الأولى ستكون بينهم وبين المسلمين فالمسلمون شرقي نهر الأردن واليهود غربي نهر الأردن، وتسقط فيها دولة اليهود ويتفرقون في بلاد الشام ويحرر بيت المقدس فيعود إلى المسلمين،

وبعد ذلك تفتح روما ونعم الفاتحون لها فيمكثون ثماني سنوات في الفتح، وفي السنة الثامنة يخرج المسيح الدجال يخرج خلة بين الشام والعراق فعاث يمينا وعاث شمالا، ويمكث في الأرض أربعين يوما، يوم كسنة ويوم كشهر ويوم كأسبوع وسائر أيامه كأيامكم،

وبعد ذلك تقع الحرب الثانية وهي الحرب مع المسيح الدجال ومن معه من اليهود يقودها المسيح بن مريم عليه السلام ينزل وقت أذان الفجر عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين ملكين إذا رفع رأسه تحدر منه مثل الجمان وإذا طأطأه تقاطر كأنما خرج من ديماس أي كأنما خرج من حمام لا يتغير لونه، لا يشك فيه أحد أنه المسيح ابن مريم، لا يحل لكافر أن يجد ريح نفسه إلا ذاب كما يذوب الملح في الماء، وإن نفسه ليبلغ ما يبلغ بصره،

فيدرك المسيح الدجال برملة لد، ورملة لد هي مطار تل ابيب الآن، باب اللد هو مطار تل ابيب الآن، فيقتله هنالك وحينئذ يكسر الصليب ويقتل الخنزير ويسقط الجزية ويقاتل معه المسلمون يهاجرون إليه من مشارق الأرض ومغاربها، وحينئذ يتكلم الحجر والشجر يا عبد الله يا مسلم هذا يهودي خلفي فتعال فاقتله إلا الغرقد فإنه من شجر اليهود، هذا في الحرب الثانية.
body_en:
Will Jerusalem be liberated, and who will liberate it, and at what time?

Yes, Jerusalem will be conquered. The Prophet, upon whom be peace, made clear that the conquest of Jerusalem occurs at the ruin of Medina, and that after it occurs the conquest of Rome, and that the Dajjal comes forth in the eighth — that is, in the eighth year after that.

So Jerusalem will be conquered in the first war with the Jews. Two wars remain for the Jews. The first war will be between them and the Muslims: the Muslims east of the River Jordan and the Jews west of the River Jordan. In it the state of the Jews will fall and they will be scattered through the lands of Syria, and Jerusalem will be liberated and will return to the Muslims.

After that, Rome will be conquered — and excellent are those who will conquer it. They will remain eight years in the conquest, and in the eighth year the False Messiah will come forth. He will come forth from a gap between Syria and Iraq, and will spread corruption to the right and spread corruption to the left. He will remain on the earth forty days: a day like a year, a day like a month, a day like a week, and the rest of his days like your days.

After that the second war will take place, the war with the False Messiah and those of the Jews who are with him, led by the Messiah son of Mary, peace be upon him. He will descend at the time of the call to the dawn prayer at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two angels. When he raises his head, there run down from him drops like pearls; and when he lowers it, they fall in drops, as though he had come out of a vaulted bath — that is, as though he had come out of a bath-house — his colour unchanging. No one will doubt that he is the Messiah son of Mary. It is not possible for an unbeliever to catch the scent of his breath without dissolving, as salt dissolves in water; and his breath reaches as far as his sight reaches.

He will overtake the False Messiah at the sandy plain of Ludd — and the sandy plain of Ludd is Tel Aviv airport today; the gate of Ludd is Tel Aviv airport today — and will kill him there. At that time he will break the cross, kill the swine and abolish the poll tax (jizyah), and the Muslims will fight alongside him, emigrating to him from the easts of the earth and its wests. And at that time the stone and the tree will speak: 'O servant of God, O Muslim, this is a Jew behind me, so come and kill him' — except the boxthorn (al-gharqad), for it is one of the trees of the Jews. This is in the second war.

flags.arabic: وتسقط فيها دولة اليهود … هذا يهودي خلفي فتعال فاقتله إلا الغرقد فإنه من شجر اليهود
options: publish with a substantial preface from the Sheikh's office setting out the genre and the sources
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW REQUIRED (style guide §12). This is the highest-risk item in this slice. It is an eschatological answer stated throughout as plain future fact, and it ends by reproducing the gharqad hadith — the tree that says 'this is a Jew behind me, come and kill him' — with no framing, no citation and no comment. It has been translated exactly as given: nothing softened, nothing strengthened, nothing added or removed, and no explanatory framing introduced by the translator. In English, detached from the hadith literature it is drawn from, this reads as incitement, and it is the sort of text that is quoted out of context. Note also that the Sheikh's identification of Ludd with Tel Aviv airport is his own contemporary gloss, not part of the reports. The decision whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office, and this item should not be shipped by default.

flags.arabic: وقد بين النبي (ص) أن فتح بيت المقدس يحصل عند خراب المدينة
flags.context: the whole chain of events is attributed to the Prophet without a single citation
options: translate as given, with no citation supplied
translate and note which reports the wording draws on
hold the item until sources are supplied
flags.note: The answer attributes a dated sequence to the Prophet — ruin of Medina, conquest of Jerusalem, conquest of Rome, Dajjal in the eighth year — and reproduces the wording of several well-known reports on the descent of Jesus and the killing of the Dajjal at Ludd. The Sheikh names no narrator, no collection and no grading anywhere in it, and none has been supplied. For a text presented as prophecy this absence is itself material, and the site should make it visible. Compare article 531, where the same sequence is given in nearly identical terms, also uncited.

flags.arabic: ورملة لد هي مطار تل ابيب الآن، باب اللد هو مطار تل ابيب الآن
flags.context: the Sheikh's identification of the place named in the reports
options: the sandy plain of Ludd — and the sandy plain of Ludd is Tel Aviv airport today
the plain of Lydda — and Lydda is where Tel Aviv airport now stands
Ramlat Ludd, which is the site of Tel Aviv airport today
flags.note: This sentence is the Sheikh's own contemporary identification, not part of the report he is relating, and the distinction must not be lost in English. The repetition (first رملة لد, then باب اللد) is in the source and has been kept. Ludd is the town of Lydda/Lod; the airport there is today Ben Gurion airport, but the Sheikh's wording has not been updated or corrected.

flags.context: وإذا طأطأه تقاطر كأنما خرج من ديماس أي كأنما خرج من حمام
options: as though he had come out of a vaulted bath
as though he had come out of a bath-house
as though he had emerged from a steam room
flags.note: ديماس is glossed by the Sheikh himself in the next breath as حمام, a bath-house, so the English keeps both his word and his gloss. Some transmissions of the report read دِيماس as a vaulted chamber or cistern rather than a bath.

translator_notes: Hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The whole answer is given in the voice of settled future fact ('yes, Jerusalem will be conquered'). No hedging has been introduced and none has been removed.

The Sheikh's own glosses inside the reports ('that is, in the eighth year after that'; 'that is, as though he had come out of a bath'; 'the sandy plain of Ludd is Tel Aviv airport today') have been kept and are distinguishable from the reported wording.

This item overlaps substantially with the first item of article 531, which gives the same sequence. The two are not identical in wording and have been translated independently; a reviewer may wish to compare them.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: تل ابيب written without the hamza, and المسيح بن مريم without the alif of ابن alongside المسيح ابن مريم with it, in the same paragraph.
dec: Reproduces the gharqad report with no framing, no citation and no comment, inside an answer stated throughout as plain future fact.
